description: A director of career and technical education must authorize the conversion of Lab 3 into a robotics laboratory and finalize its capacity, electrical preparation, network configuration, and funding documentation, with input from the robotics teacher, facilities manager, information technology coordinator, and finance officer.

agents.name: Dr. Morgan
agents.role: Director of Career and Technical Education

shared_context.S1: The school plans to convert Lab 3 into a robotics laboratory for the next academic year.
shared_context.S2: The draft conversion request proposes 12 student workstations and use of the existing room infrastructure.
shared_context.S3: The robotics equipment vendor requires power, network connectivity, and a documented funding source before delivering the equipment.
shared_context.S4: Dr. Morgan has authority to approve the conversion and its operating conditions.
shared_context.S5: As part of the school's normal pre-approval process, Dr. Morgan holds a review with the robotics teacher, facilities manager, information technology coordinator, and finance officer before issuing the decision.

PF1.text: Ms. Bell's confirmed course roster contains 16 students for the first robotics section, and district practice requires one workstation per student; she finalized the roster this week but the conversion request still lists 12 stations.

PF2.text: A facilities inspection found that Lab 3's existing circuit is only 20 amps; the robotics equipment requires a dedicated 240-volt circuit, and Mr. Ortiz confirmed the electrical requirement during the inspection this week but has not added it to the request.

PF3.text: The robotics kits require a district-secure IoT network with wired drops because the ordinary student Wi-Fi cannot support their device-management protocol; Ms. Shah verified this against the vendor's technical specifications this week but the network field remains blank.

PF4.text: A workforce-development grant has awarded exactly $18,500 for this conversion, restricted to capital infrastructure and equipment preparation; Mr. Greene received the executed award notice this week but has not entered it in the project ledger.

acceptance_conditions: The conversion plan must specify 16 student workstations.
A dedicated 240-volt circuit must be included in the approved plan.
The laboratory must use the district-secure IoT network with wired drops.
The conversion must be funded by exactly $18,500 from the workforce-development grant.
The settlement must include an electrical-upgrade commitment.
The settlement must include a secure-network installation commitment.
The settlement must include a grant-ledger documentation commitment.

content_checks.C3: 'district-secure IoT network with wired drops' in decisions['network_configuration'] or 'District-secure IoT network with wired drops' in decisions['network_configuration']
content_checks.C4: ('workforce-development grant' in decisions['funding_source'] or 'Workforce-development grant' in decisions['funding_source']) and decisions['funding_amount'] == 18500
content_checks.C5: any('dedicated 240-volt circuit' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any('district-secure IoT network with wired drops' in c['detail'] or 'District-secure IoT network with wired drops' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('$18,500' in c['detail'] and 'project ledger' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The confirmed roster changes the required workstation count from the draft 12 to exactly 16.
The inspection changes the infrastructure decision from using the existing circuit to installing a dedicated 240-volt circuit and documenting that upgrade.
The vendor specification changes the network choice from unspecified or ordinary Wi-Fi to the district-secure IoT network with wired drops and requires an installation commitment.
The executed award changes the funding entry to exactly $18,500 from the workforce-development grant and requires the amount to be recorded in the project ledger.
